title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not part of the cycle-theory notes around it, which deal with Albanese varieties and A_0. It is page 25 of a typescript of SGA 3, Exposé XIV ('Éléments réguliers : suite. Application aux groupes algébriques'), with Grothendieck's handwritten corrections. It was evidently misfiled in cote 14. The marginal note 'Conserver le texte ci-contre, barré par erreur' is an instruction to the typist: keep the boxed text that was struck out by mistake.

Mathematics.
- Let G be a smooth connected algebraic group over a field k and let 𝒯 be the scheme of maximal tori of G. It is isomorphic to the scheme of Cartan subgroups, via T ↦ C = Centralizer(T).
- Send each regular point g to the unique Cartan subgroup containing it. This gives a morphism U → 𝒯 from the dense open set U of regular points of G.
- The fibres are the dense open subsets of regular points inside the Cartan subgroups of the fibres of G_𝒯.
- Passing to the generic point gives Corollary 3.3. The function field k(G) = k(U) is k(𝒯)-isomorphic to the function field of the generic Cartan subgroup C. C is a smooth connected affine nilpotent group over k(𝒯), namely the Cartan subgroup of G_{k(𝒯)} that is the generic fibre over 𝒯.
- If G is affine of reductive (unipotent) rank zero, the Cartan subgroups of G_{k̄} are tori. Then C is a k(𝒯)-torus and k(G) is unirational over k(𝒯).

The last step uses Chevalley's lemma that a torus T over k is unirational:
- Choose a finite separable extension k'/k that splits T. Then T_{k'} is rational.
- Hence the Weil restriction R_{k'/k}(T_{k'}) is rational, since it contains a dense open set of R_{k'/k}(E^n_{k'}) ≅ E^{n[k':k]}_k.
- The norm map R_{k'/k}(T_{k'}) → T is dominant (the page breaks off before this step).

What it serves: the theorem of SGA 3 XIV that every connected reductive group over an arbitrary field, including imperfect fields, is unirational. This extends Chevalley's and Borel–Springer's results. The full argument also needs 𝒯 to be rational over k, which is part of what 'l'exposé suivant' will refine.
errors: 'fibre générique de X au dessus de 𝒯': X is a stray letter. It should be U, or the family of Cartan subgroups of G_𝒯.

Unirationality of k(G) over k(𝒯) alone does not give unirationality of G over k. One also needs the rationality or unirationality of 𝒯, treated elsewhere in SGA 3 XIV. Not an error, but a gap on this page.
The original typed hypothesis 'rang unipotent nul' without 'affine' was imprecise. Grothendieck corrects it by hand to 'G est affine de rang unipotent nul' and specifies Cartan subgroups 'de G_{k̄}'.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a misfiled draft page of SGA 3 Exp. XIV. Its content (generic Cartan subgroup, unirationality of reductive groups) is published and credited to Grothendieck and Chevalley. The only archival interest is the misfiling and the editorial annotations.
transcription_corrections: The page is a typescript of SGA 3 Exp. XIV, p. 25, not part of the cycle notes; the handwritten '126' is the archive foliation.
The first line '[-obtenues par extensions du corps de base-]' is a struck-out typed line.
'les fibres étant [-géométriques-]': 'géométriques' is a struck word written above the line, followed by another struck handwritten word.
Margin note reads: 'Conserver le texte ci-contre, barré par erreur', referring to the boxed Lemma 3.4 and its proof.
'de X au dessus de 𝒯' is as typed; X is a typo in the original.
Handwritten insertion: 'le résultat bien connu suivant (dû à Chevalley)'.
